title: Financial Management
overview: A solid understanding of financial management is essential for making strategic and operational business decisions. Leaders and managers across all organizational levels must speak the language of finance to build credibility and effectively communicate with finance managers and executives. This knowledge is equally critical for finance and accounting professionals to advance their careers and make sound decisions.

This comprehensive Financial Management course equips participants with the financial terminology, concepts, and tools required to analyze financial statements, evaluate business performance, and present persuasive business proposals. Through a blend of theoretical and practical approaches, participants will gain the confidence to navigate the complexities of financial management.
audience: This course is designed for finance professionals, finance managers, corporate controllers, financial controllers, treasury professionals, chief accountants, accounting managers, senior accountants, banking professionals, and corporate business leaders.
methodology: The course employs an interactive mix of methodologies, including expert-led presentations, group exercises, Excel-based case studies, and hands-on projects. Participants will present their findings to demonstrate their grasp of the subject matter.
objectivesIntro: By the end of the course, participants will be able to:
objectives: Apply core principles of corporate financial management.
Integrate strategic and operational perspectives into macro financial roles.
Develop a practical understanding of corporate finance, capital budgeting, and the cost of capital.
Compare pricing mechanisms for equities and fixed-income securities.
Build strategic financial planning models for dynamic decision-making.
Explain the fundamentals of mergers, acquisitions, takeovers, and corporate control.

outline.title: 1. The Scope of Corporate Financial Management

items.text: The three pillars of financial management

Liquidity, solvency, efficiency, and profitability analysis

items.text: Net present value (NPV) as a decision-making tool
Calculating the weighted average cost of capital (WACC)
